blocks.text: The next time Seth climbed to Jenny’s roof, he stopped at the door and listened. No clangs. No shouting from the street. Jenny stood beside the brick wall in her pink and white suit, looking out toward Terminal Tower.
He had slept properly. He had even remembered to straighten his red mask before coming upstairs. The steel drum was still where they had left it.
Jenny glanced at it when she heard him. “Ready for the rematch?”
“I was hoping it had retired.”
She laughed, then looked over the wall again. Seth joined her, leaving the drum alone. The lake was pale beyond the buildings. Below them, traffic waited at a light.
“Still thinking about the truck?” he asked.
“What if someone had been behind it?” She turned her white-gloved hands over.
Seth rested his elbows on the wall. “Yeah. That drum could’ve gone over the edge, too.” He glanced at her. “I just wanted you to see me lift it.”
“I saw.”
“All of it, unfortunately.”
Her smile returned, but she let him finish.
“Everybody keeps calling us heroes. I feel like I’m supposed to know what I’m doing.”
Jenny watched the traffic begin moving. “You think I do? I didn’t even wait to hear what Flaming Head was saying.”
Seth looked at her. He had imagined she felt certain most of the time. She had sounded certain when she told people where to go during the fight. Now she was worrying about her hands.

blocks.alt: In their full costumes, Jenny and Seth share a quiet conversation beside the brick wall on her apartment rooftop, with Cleveland’s Terminal Tower beyond them.
blocks.text: “You don’t have to pretend you’ve got it figured out. Not with me,” he said. Jenny leaned beside him, close enough for their elbows to touch. For a little while, neither of them tried to fill the silence.
Flaming Head rose into view above the stairwell. He looked from them to the practice space and waited until they turned around.
They began with Seth’s lift. Jenny stood clear of the drum. This time she did not cheer when it rose.
Seth brought it above his head and held it there. He knew she was watching. The thought made him want to glance at her, but he kept his eyes on the drum.
“No hurry,” she said. “I’m not going anywhere.”
He lowered it slowly. The base touched the roof without a clang.
Only then did he look at her.

blocks.alt: Seth holds the steel drum steadily overhead, then lowers it safely to the rooftop. Jenny gives him a proud thumbs-up while Flaming Head smiles.
blocks.text: “That’s more like it,” Jenny said, giving him a thumbs-up. With the drum safely on the roof, Seth let himself grin.
He lifted it again. On the third attempt, his attention wandered toward a horn below. He noticed the drum beginning to tilt and set it down before he lost his grip.
Flaming Head nodded. Seth took a break. There was no need to turn a wobble into another accident.
For Jenny’s practice, they moved the drum in front of a broad brick wall, facing away from the street. Seth stepped well aside. Flaming Head watched the space between her boots and the target.
Jenny started moving her legs. When the light appeared, she stiffened. Her rhythm broke, and the small glow vanished.
She let her feet settle. Seth waited.
“Aren’t you going to tell me to try again?” she asked.
“When you’re ready.”
Jenny took another breath. She looked at the drum before she began, choosing the place she wanted to hit. Then her boots blurred again.
The plasma gathered into a small ball. She kept her eyes on the target, planted one foot and gave it a short kick.

blocks.alt: A rear three-quarter view of Jenny in her full pink-and-white costume as she practices a controlled plasma kick toward the steel drum on the Cleveland rooftop.
blocks.text: It struck the drum with a bright flare. A black mark remained on the steel. Nothing went over the roof.
Jenny stood still, staring at the mark. Then she turned toward Seth.

blocks.alt: Jenny’s controlled plasma kick strikes the steel drum target on the rooftop. Afterward, she and Seth celebrate with a high-five beside the scorched drum while Flaming Head smiles.
blocks.text: He grinned. She grinned back and raised her white-gloved hand. Seth met it with a high-five. Behind them, Flaming Head smiled at the scorched drum.
Her next kick went wide and scorched the brick beside the drum. They checked the practice space before continuing.
By the time the windows below began reflecting the evening sky, Seth had made several steady lifts and Jenny had hit the drum again. They stopped while they could still pay attention.
At the stairwell, Jenny caught his hand. “Same time tomorrow?”
Seth nodded. He looked down at their gloves for a moment, then back at her. This time, he managed to answer without trying to think of something impressive.
“I’ll be here.”
